summary: Comprehensive backend testing for MailCtl. Ran 26 pytest cases covering auth (register/login/me/logout/brute-force), domains (CRUD/DNS/verify/cascade), mailboxes, aliases, relays (incl. default exclusivity + secret masking), send/test (failed-log path), retry/delete logs, stats, deliverability, and multi-tenant isolation. After fixing 2 backend bugs (datetime tz compare in brute-force lockout, missing _id pop on insert_one for mailboxes/aliases/relays), 26/26 tests pass.

critical.issue: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes when checking locked_until — caused 500 instead of 429 once lockout was active. FIXED by coercing locked_until to UTC-aware before comparison.

After `await db.<col>.insert_one(doc)`, motor mutates the dict to include `_id` ObjectId. The handler returned the same dict, causing FastAPI serialization to fail with 500 ('ObjectId' object is not iterable). FIXED by popping `_id` from the returned doc in all three create routes.

minor.issue: Performance: runs synchronous dnspython queries inside a request handler for every domain serially. For users with many domains, this will block. Consider asyncio.gather + executor or background job.
Field `total_logs` is set from `delivery_logs.count_documents({"user_id": uid})` but named variable is `verified_count`, which is confusing/misleading. Cosmetic refactor.
Does not rotate refresh token; only re-issues access. Acceptable but worth noting for security review.
`secure=False` on cookies (auth.py). Acceptable for self-hosted HTTP, but on the preview HTTPS domain browser will still accept lax+non-secure. Document for production hardening.

Reuses original `provider_id` even if that relay was deleted. If provider was deleted, retry currently goes through default-relay path (relay_id passed but find_one returns None → 404). Not tested in detail.

action_items: Review the 2 fixes I applied (auth_routes.py tz handling, _id pop in mail_routes.py/relay_routes.py).
Decide on retry policy when underlying provider has been deleted (currently 404).
Consider awaiting DNS lookups in a thread pool for /api/deliverability so a large fleet of domains doesn't block the worker.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG: relay_routes.py PATCH `is_default` exclusivity — when toggling on, the update_many runs before update_one, but if the patched relay isn't found (404), other relays were already flipped off. Should reorder or check existence first.

BUG/STRUCTURE: `_attempt_send` does not catch unexpected exceptions raised by services.relay_service.send_email. Need defensive `try/except` so a single bad provider doesn't 500 the request before logging.
Design: `_user_out` is duplicated logic (compare with get_current_user shaping). Consolidate into a single util.
Security: `secure=False` cookie flag should be env-driven (`COOKIE_SECURE=true` in prod).
Code-quality: `domains.py` `verify_domain` and `deliverability_routes.deliverability` share identical scoring/update logic — extract a helper to avoid drift.

Code-quality: `routers/relay_routes.py` `retry_log` calls `send_test_email` re-entrantly with the dict user object — works but bypasses Pydantic; mark with comment or refactor to call inner _send function.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@example.com / admin123 (seeded). Test users created on-the-fly with unique emails per run.
seed_data_creation: Each test run registers fresh users (test_a_*, test_b_*, test_reg_*, test_dup_*, test_bf_*) and creates throwaway domains/mailboxes/aliases/relays scoped to those users. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 26 backend pytest cases pass after the 2 backend fixes (datetime tz + _id pop). Re-running `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v` should still show 26 passed. Frontend was not tested per request. If revisiting backend, run the suite as a regression. The brute-force test will leave one IP+email pair locked for 15 min; tests use a unique email each run so it's idempotent.
rca_of_the_issue:
Two backend defects discovered:
1) Brute-force lockout 500: locked_until persisted by motor came back as naive datetime; comparing against tz-aware now() raised TypeError -> 500. Reproduce: 5 wrong passwords for the same email/IP, 6th call. Fix: coerce naive → UTC-aware before compare.
2) 500 on mailbox/alias/relay create: motor's insert_one mutates the input dict to add _id (ObjectId). Returning the dict tripped FastAPI's jsonable_encoder which can't serialize ObjectId. Reproduce: any POST to /api/mailboxes /api/aliases /api/relays. Fix: pop _id from doc before returning, or build a clean response dict.
